clue.text: The fellow leading soldiers up — a courageous man

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece leads, coming before the next one

parts.note: a fellow is referred to as he

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for soldiers is written bottom to top

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A man walks at the head of a column of troops and shows bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OR into RO beneath HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion of bravery, someone admired for courage, is the classic sense of the word.

clue.text: Very sad end for establishment with smoke rising

indicators.note: the end for a word is its final letter, here taken from establishment
in a down entry, rising means the word for smoke is read upwards

parts.note: a cigar is something you smoke

explanation.surface: A sorry closing scene for a building that has smoke going up from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoke' looks like a noun for fumes, but here it is a thing you smoke; 'rising' reads it upwards, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous or heartbreaking is described with this adjective, a synonym for very sad.

clue.text: The second character is one of the little women

definitions.meaning: the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet
... March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: Second in line among the girls of a famous family novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Hebrew alphabet's second letter and a March sister in Little Women.

clue.text: Put back nearly all the bits of the bookcase?

indicators.note: nearly all means the last letter of the word for the bookcase parts is dropped

parts.note: the horizontal boards in a bookcase on which books stand

explanation.surface: Someone returns books to almost every ledge of a bookcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as returning books to a shelf, but it means postpone.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone or defer a plan is to put it back, the verb's idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Portray footballer as a nuisance

parts.note: to portray in pictures is to draw
a back is a defensive player in football

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a football player as an annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage or snag is an inconvenience, close to a nuisance.

clue.text: Match being held inside cannot upset competitor

indicators.note: being held inside means the match word sits within the scrambled letters
upset means the letters of cannot are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A game played indoors, and someone who cannot cope gets upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of 'cannot', and 'being held inside' sits the cricket Test within them; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking part in a game or contest is a rival or entrant.

clue.text: Live next to farmland? That can be put up with

definitions.text: That can be put up with

indicators.note: next to means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
arable land is farmland used for crops

explanation.surface: Living beside fields that are ploughed is something one can tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerable or endurable is something that can be put up with.

clue.text: Forbidden to go wild? Not in county town

indicators.note: to go wild means the letters of forbidden are thrown into disorder
Not means the letters of in are left out of the scramble

explanation.surface: Is running riot banned? Not in a certain English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go wild' and 'Not in' together: FORBIDDEN rearranged with I and N removed gives the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedford is the county town, the administrative seat, of Bedfordshire in England.

clue.text: School hurt endlessly by quarrel

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word for hurt is cut

parts.note: to hurt is to harm
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A school pupil is wounded over and over by a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public (private boarding) school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow School is one of England's best-known independent schools.

clue.text: Dog led off to be put in kennel, say?

indicators.note: off means the letters of dog led go awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog is led away to be housed in a kennel.
explanation.definitionFit: To be housed or accommodated somewhere, as a dog in a kennel is, by way of example.

clue.text: Approve of what twit here can be seen to do

parts.note: the two words twit here contain the four letters w-i-t-h running together, so they can be said to hold them

explanation.surface: A sarcastic question about whether one agrees with what some fool is doing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer means 'contain the letters W-I-T-H', which the words 'twit here' visibly do; the rest of the clue just points at what those words do.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree with or support an idea is idiomatically to go along with it, to approve of it.

clue.text: 'Customers,' I plea, 'must get special treatment. They are very valuable!'

indicators.note: special treatment means the letters of customers and I plea are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper begs that regular customers be pampered because they are precious to the business.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold, silver and platinum are prized for their worth, so valuable is their defining feature.

clue.text: Classical poetry with phrases I'd translated about love

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the love symbol
translated means the letters of phrases I'd are turned into a fresh form

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: Ancient verse in which the speaker has rendered lines concerning romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges PHRASESID, and 'about' puts that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece these were epic poems, or sections of them, recited by a bard.

clue.text: Ointment not to waste left hidden

indicators.note: the left letter is tucked away inside the word for not wasting

parts.note: to avoid wasting something is to save it

explanation.surface: A cream that should be used up, the leftover tucked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' here puts L inside SAVE rather than signalling a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing balm or healing cream applied to skin is a synonym for ointment.

clue.text: Tense with father and son getting agreement finally

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of agreement

explanation.surface: Father and son are on edge until they finally come to terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the pair, but it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The past is a grammatical tense, one of the verb forms showing time.

clue.text: Volunteers covering a little land down under, a province, and an African country

indicators.note: covering means the volunteers' letters wrap round the following pieces

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
NZ is the short form of New Zealand, a land down under; little marks the abbreviation
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers serve in New Zealand, a British province and Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' means the Territorial Army's letters split to enclose the rest; Northern Ireland is often called simply the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanzania is a nation of East Africa, bordering Kenya and the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Pottery expert bringing learner aboard

indicators.note: aboard means the learner's letter is taken on inside the word for expert

parts.note: deft means skilful, expert
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A skilled potter takes on an apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is tin-glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of Delft, so the name denotes a pottery.

clue.text: Little kid facing monstrous mice is sending a message

indicators.note: in a down entry, facing means the first piece stands before the second

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: monstrous means the letters of mice are deformed into another order

explanation.surface: A toddler confronting horrible mice is trying to say something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monstrous' signals the letters of 'mice' rearranged; 'facing' just places the small child first. A totem is an emblem, so totemic things carry a symbolic message.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emblematic or symbolic carries meaning, conveying a signal about what it stands for.

clue.text: A knight trailing behind king, hard ruler

indicators.note: trailing behind means the a-and-knight pair comes after the king and hard letters

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight lags behind a monarch who is a stern ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is a title for a sovereign or chief in Central Asia, such as Genghis.

clue.text: Soppiness conveyed by one way of thinking

parts.note: sent means dispatched, conveyed
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mentality is a mindset, a way of thinking

explanation.surface: Mawkishness transmitted by a particular outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive tender emotion, being mawkish or maudlin, is what soppiness means.

clue.text: One gets cold and anxious, no end, when it's freezing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: no end means the last letter of the word for anxious is lost

parts.note: eager means keen, anxious to do something

explanation.surface: Someone catches a chill and frets endlessly in icy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial period is an era of long, deep cold, a time when the world is freezing.

clue.text: Around five the French worker gets to bunk off

indicators.note: around means the French article and the worker go about the numeral

parts.note: le is French for the
an ant is a worker insect
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: At about five o'clock a French labourer skives off work.
explanation.walkthrough: To levant is a dated British verb: to run off leaving debts unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond, sneak away to avoid obligations, is what bunk off means in British slang.

clue.text: Next door there's a player of records needing a bit of money

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, plays records
a cent is a small coin, a bit of money

explanation.surface: The neighbours have a disc jockey who is short of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjoining or neighbouring places sit beside each other, the sense of next door.

clue.text: Quality of gem perhaps initially not evident

indicators.note: initially not evident means the first letter of the word for gem goes missing

parts.note: a gem is an example of a precious stone

explanation.surface: How good a jewel is may not be obvious at first glance.
explanation.definitionFit: The character or timbre of a sound is its quality, as with a voice or instrument.

clue.text: Changing address may be generating strong feelings

definitions.meaning: relocating from one home to another

explanation.surface: Relocating home can be an emotional experience.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both relocating house and being emotionally stirring or touching.

clue.text: Reportedly recognises organ

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for recognises is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to recognise someone is to know them, giving knows

explanation.surface: Word has it that someone can identify a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelling organ of the face is one of the body's sense organs.

clue.text: Margaret, having secured victory, is making high-pitched cry

indicators.note: having secured means the short form of Margaret holds the victory word inside it

parts.note: Meg is a short form of the name Margaret
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Margaret, after clinching a win, lets out a shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats and gulls give a thin plaintive call, a mew, so this is uttering a high-pitched cry.

clue.text: Precision of a Christian creed laid down by saints

indicators.note: laid down by means the creed is placed next to the saints' letters

parts.note: the Nicene Creed is a statement of Christian belief

explanation.surface: The exactness of a Christian statement of faith established by holy figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means fine or subtle, so this noun means exactness, a fine distinction.
